title: Day 964: Knesset Panel Restores Word 'Massacre' to Oct. 7 Memorial Bill After Backlash; 34 Days to Supreme Court July 1 Accountability Deadline
detail: On May 28, 2026 (Day 964 / Ceasefire Day 231), a Knesset committee panel restored the word 'massacre' to the October 7 Memorial Day bill after public and political backlash over its initial removal. The bill, which establishes an annual state memorial day to commemorate the October 7, 2023 attack, had been revised in committee — with the word 'massacre' stripped from key language — prompting immediate condemnation from bereaved families, opposition parties, and media commentators who called the edit 'a deliberate erasure of the horror.' The panel's reversal restored the original language, though the incident underscored the ongoing political sensitivity surrounding official terminology for the October 7 attacks within the Israeli legislative process. Concurrently, the broader accountability crisis continued its countdown: 34 days remain until the Israeli Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 constitutional deadline for the government to present a 'suitable framework' for investigating October 7. The High Court of Justice had described the 32-month absence of any formal independent probe as 'unacceptable.' The Knesset coalition's Kallner inquiry bill — which dropped 'full, thorough, and independent investigation' from its purpose clause and bars Supreme Court justices from membership — continues its legislative path toward a first full Knesset plenum reading. Opposition parties have pledged an immediate Supreme Court challenge if the bill passes, arguing it fails the minimum independence threshold the High Court has set. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara previously described the revised bill as 'tailor-made for the government's personal needs.' The October Council (bereaved families' forum) maintained weekly protests outside the Prime Minister's residence, with families of the 1,195 victims demanding a genuine independent commission with subpoena power. The Beyachad alliance (Naftali Bennett + Yair Lapid) continued to poll as the leading opposition bloc, with an independent October 7 state commission as their pledged Day 1 governing priority. 72% of Israelis (Hebrew University poll, April 2026) and 63% (JPPI, May 15) favor an independent inquiry. Phase Two of the Gaza ceasefire (Hamas disarmament and Israeli withdrawal) remained in total deadlock on Ceasefire Day 231.

title: Day 964: Hamas Gaza City Deputy Commander Imad Aslim and Northern Gaza Brigade Commander Izz al-Din Beck Confirmed Killed in May 27 IDF Strikes; Funerals Held May 28 as Hamas Military Succession Vacuum Deepens
detail: On May 28, 2026 (Day 964 / Ceasefire Day 231), Hamas-affiliated media reported the funerals of Imad Aslim — deputy commander of Hamas's Gaza City brigade — and Izz al-Din Beck — commander of Hamas's northern Gaza brigade — both killed in separate IDF targeted strikes on May 27, 2026. Their killings occurred on the same day as IDF airstrike that eliminated Hamas Al-Qassam Brigades overall commander Mohammed Odeh in the Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City. The Aslim/Beck strikes were part of a series of IDF operations on Eid al-Adha (May 27–28) targeting multiple Hamas field commanders simultaneously. The dual confirmation deepens Hamas's military succession vacuum: within a single two-week window (May 15–27, 2026), Israel eliminated three successive Hamas commanders — Izz al-Din al-Haddad (overall military wing head), Mohammed Odeh (his replacement, killed 9 days later), and now two Hamas brigade-level commanders. As of May 28, no new Hamas Al-Qassam Brigades supreme commander had been publicly announced. The systematic targeting represents a direct continuation of Israel's NILI task force (Shin Bet + Mossad joint unit, revealed by the Wall Street Journal on May 21–22, 2026), which maintains a comprehensive database of all approximately 3,000 October 7 participants for kill-or-capture operations. According to a Ynet report on May 28, at least one pre-October 7 senior Hamas Gaza figure remained alive — described as a 'shadowy commander' who had survived Israel's systematic targeting campaign. IDF strikes continued throughout Eid al-Adha, with Israeli operations killing at least 10 people in overnight strikes on al-Rimal, Gaza City (including four children). The Gaza Government Media Office documented 3,005+ Israeli ceasefire violations since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire began. All 251 October 7 hostages have been accounted for since January 26, 2026.

media.caption: NBC News — IDF kills Hamas military commanders; succession vacuum deepens after Odeh killing; funerals held May 28
